courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Research in the Agricultural Sciences
courses.description: Principles, tools and techniques used in scientific research as applied to the agricultural sciences. Topics will include the development of literature reviews and annotated bibliographies, appropriate literature citation, online research methods and sources, the identification and definition of a research topic and its rationale. Readings, discussions, computer applications, and research.

courses.title: Research Design and Data Analysis for Agriculture
courses.description: Introduction and application of different statistic methods required for the graduate research such as regression, correlation, one and two-way ANOVA with post-hoc tests, Chi-square, and SAS. The basics of design of experiments, such as least factorial design of experiments, hypothesis testing, mean comparisons, regressions and multivariate statistical analysis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research Proposal
courses.description: The format and content of research proposals and scientific communication culminating with the student’s Master’s thesis research proposal. The student will develop the justification and rationale for the research through a focused review, will develop hypotheses and experimental approaches for testing each hypothesis. Learn to communicate the scientific content of their thesis research to scientists and effectively communicate the same to lay audiences. This will be accomplished through written assignments and PowerPoint presentations.
courses.prerequisites: AG 500 or AG 5100 ; and thesis research project chosen.

courses.title: Youth and Adult Leadership Programs
courses.description: Organization, history, philosophy, administration and procedures in advising of the Future Farmers Association (FFA) chapters and conducting classes for out-of-school youth and adults. Surveys and plans for development of rural and urban adult programs, FFA and Young Farmer programs, techniques and methods.

courses.title: Agricultural Science Internship
courses.description: Individualized study, research, or readings in a specialized area under the direction of a faculty member. Maybe be taken up to two times for total credit of 4 units.

courses.title: Program Planning and Development
courses.description: Study of career opportunities in agriculture. Program development in such areas as the Future Farmers of America, and other youth groups. Supervised practice including cooperative work experience in agriculture. Development of up-to-date approaches in an integrated program. Operating policies and procedures.

courses.title: Procedures in Agricultural Education
courses.description: Approaches to the learning process and development of daily and unit plans as well as the utilization of resources. Class demonstration in teaching procedures with emphasis being given to lesson development, micro-teaching, and the development of pedagogical skills including development analysis, assessment and evaluation.

courses.title: Procedures in Agricultural Education Activity

courses.title: Specialized Studies in Agricultural Science

courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Maybe taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.

courses.title: Comprehensive Exam
courses.description: Preparation for and completion of the written comprehensive examination. The examination may be taken no more than two times. Failure to complete exam satisfactorily the second time will result in termination from the program.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
